title: Annihilator of a finite module commutes with localization at an element
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $f\in A$, and $M$ a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], with annihilator $\operatorname{Ann}_A(M)=\{a\in A: am=0\text{ for all }m\in M\}$. Let $A_f$ be the localization of $A$ at $f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and $M_f$ the localization of $M$ at $f$, an $A_f$-module [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Then $\operatorname{Ann}_{A_f}(M_f)=\operatorname{Ann}_A(M)A_f$, the ideal of $A_f$ generated by the elements $a/1$, $a\in\operatorname{Ann}_A(M)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 07T8 (algebra-lemma-annihilator-flat-base-change), second assertion, for the flat ring map A -> A_f (Algebra, Lemma 00HT algebra-lemma-flat-localization), with M (x)_A A_f = M_f; its proof uses Lemma 0BBY (algebra-lemma-flat-intersect-ideals). This special case is the 'algebra fact' that the proof of Morphisms, Lemma 05JU (morphisms-lemma-scheme-theoretic-support) states and omits.

proof.text: *Step 1 ($\operatorname{Ann}_A(M)A_f\subseteq\operatorname{Ann}_{A_f}(M_f)$).* $\operatorname{Ann}_{A_f}(M_f)$ is an ideal of $A_f$: if $x,y$ kill every element of $M_f$ and $z\in A_f$, so do $x+y$ and $zx$, by the module axioms of $M_f$. Let $a\in\operatorname{Ann}_A(M)$. Every element of $M_f$ is $m/f^e$ with $m\in M$, $e\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], and by the rule $(x/f^d)(m/f^e)=xm/f^{d+e}$ of that definition, $(a/1)(m/f^e)=am/f^e=0/f^e=0$. So $a/1\in\operatorname{Ann}_{A_f}(M_f)$ for every $a\in\operatorname{Ann}_A(M)$, and the ideal $\operatorname{Ann}_A(M)A_f$ of $A_f$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] generated by these elements is contained in the ideal $\operatorname{Ann}_{A_f}(M_f)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 07T8 (lemma-annihilator-flat-base-change), second assertion, the inclusion Ann_R(M)S into Ann_S(M (x)_R S), here written out for S = A_f with M (x)_A A_f = M_f

proof.text: *Step 2 (reduction to generators).* Let $m_1,\dots,m_r$ generate $M$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then $\operatorname{Ann}_A(M)=\bigcap_k\operatorname{Ann}_A(m_k)$: an $a$ with $am_k=0$ for all $k$ kills every $\sum_ja_jm_j$. The elements $m_k/1$ generate the $A_f$-module $M_f$: an element of $M_f$ is $m/f^e=(1/f^e)(m/1)$, and writing $m=\sum_ja_jm_j$, $m/1=\sum_j(a_j/1)(m_j/1)$ since $M\to M_f$, $m\mapsto m/1$, is $A$-linear and $a\cdot(m/1)=(a/1)(m/1)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. Hence likewise $\operatorname{Ann}_{A_f}(M_f)=\bigcap_k\operatorname{Ann}_{A_f}(m_k/1)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 07T8, proof: 'If m_1, ..., m_n is a set of generators of M then Ann_R(M) = \bigcap Ann_R(m_i). Similarly Ann_S(M (x)_R S) = \bigcap Ann_S(m_i (x) 1)'

proof.text: *Step 3 (reverse inclusion).* Write x = a/s with s in the powers of f. For every m in M, x kills m/1; fraction multiplication and the localization equality criterion give t in the powers of f with t(am) = 0. Choose a finite generating set g of M. Induction on g multiplies these denominators to obtain a single t in the powers of f killing am for every generator m: on adjoining a generator with denominator u, replace t by ut; commutativity preserves the old vanishings and kills the new generator. The empty set uses t = 1. By the annihilator-of-span criterion, ta annihilates all M. The localized-ideal membership criterion then gives a/s in Ann_A(M) A_f. This uses def-weil-finitely-generated-module, def-weil-ring-localization-away and def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away. The product of powers gives their summed exponent, in place of the maximum exponent in the original plan.
